content.value_statement: Inconsistent domain terms create unclear requirements and fragile boundaries. This skill builds a shared glossary, maps contexts, and records consequential decisions.
actual_capabilities: Identifies vague, overloaded, or conflicting terms in domain discussions.
Creates and updates concise CONTEXT.md glossaries with preferred and avoided terms.
Distinguishes single-context repositories from repositories with multiple bounded contexts.
Stress-tests domain relationships with concrete edge-case scenarios.
Creates concise ADRs for consequential, surprising, and difficult-to-reverse decisions.
limitations: It requires user input or repository evidence to resolve ambiguous domain meanings.
It does not replace interviews with domain experts or stakeholder validation.
It does not produce implementation specifications or detailed technical designs.
It only recommends ADRs when a decision meets all stated significance criteria.

use_cases.title: Align Product Language
use_cases.description: Resolve conflicting business terms and create a concise shared glossary before refining requirements.

use_cases.title: Define Service Boundaries
use_cases.description: Map bounded contexts and describe their ownership and relationships during system design.

use_cases.title: Preserve Decision Context
use_cases.description: Record important architecture choices and their rationale in short, focused ADRs.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Domain Glossary
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these business terms: [terms]. Propose precise definitions, identify overlaps, and draft the first CONTEXT.md glossary.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner task for a project without an established domain glossary.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Conflicting Terms
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare our discussion with the existing CONTEXT.md. List conflicts, ask focused questions, and update resolved definitions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate task for maintaining a shared project language.

prompt_templates.title: Map Bounded Contexts
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these modules and workflows: [details]. Propose bounded contexts, ownership boundaries, relationships, and terms that need clarification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced task for a repository with several business areas.

prompt_templates.title: Stress-Test a Model and Record Decisions
prompt_templates.prompt: Challenge this domain model with edge cases: [model]. Refine ambiguous concepts and draft ADRs only for decisions meeting all qualification criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced task combining model validation with selective architecture documentation.

output_examples.input: Clarify whether account means a customer organization or a login identity.
output_examples.output: Use Customer for the purchasing organization and User for a person with login access. Avoid Account because it combines distinct concepts.

output_examples.input: Map Ordering, Billing, and Fulfillment as separate business areas.
output: Ordering owns order placement and emits OrderPlaced.
Fulfillment consumes OrderPlaced and owns picking and shipment.
Billing consumes ShipmentDispatched and owns invoice generation.

output_examples.input: Document why the system uses domain events instead of synchronous service calls.
output_examples.output: Ordering and Billing communicate through domain events. This preserves context autonomy and accepts delayed consistency in exchange for reduced runtime coupling.

best_practices: Validate each proposed definition against concrete business scenarios and repository evidence.
Keep glossary entries short, domain-specific, and free from implementation details.
Create ADRs only for difficult-to-reverse decisions with real alternatives and non-obvious rationale.
anti_patterns: Do not use one term for distinct concepts or several terms for the same concept.
Do not turn CONTEXT.md into a technical specification, scratchpad, or implementation guide.
Do not create ADRs for routine, reversible, or obvious choices.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates or updates domain glossaries, context maps, and concise architecture decision records.

faq.question: Does it support multiple bounded contexts?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses CONTEXT-MAP.md to locate contexts and describe their relationships.

faq.question: Will it inspect existing code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare code behavior with stated domain rules and surface contradictions.

faq.question: Does CONTEXT.md contain implementation details?
faq.answer: No. CONTEXT.md is a domain glossary and should exclude implementation decisions.

faq.question: When does it create an ADR?
faq.answer: It proposes an ADR only for consequential, surprising decisions that resulted from a real trade-off.

faq.question: Can it replace a domain expert?
faq.answer: No. It structures questions and documentation, but domain experts must validate business meaning.
